text:
eva: hey team, first week—trying to provision a dev cluster in eu-west1 but terraform errors mentioning quota/permissions. `gcloud compute regions describe eu-west1` returns permission denied. any day-1 checklist?

cloud-onboard-bot: Welcome! Please ensure you completed the Cloud Access form (https://go/redwood-cloud-access) and included region+APIs needed. If urgent, ping @eng-ops with project id and service account.

ops-lee: quick questions: which project are you working in and are you impersonating a SA? often new projects are created under the wrong billing folder which blocks EU quotas.

eva: project: redwood-dev-sandbox. i'm using my user creds, not impersonating SA yet. terraform plan fails at `google_compute_subnetwork` with `403: Quota 'IN_USE_ADDRESSES' exceeded` and `Permission 'resourcemanager.projects.get' denied`.

marta: two separate issues there. quota means project isn't in EU billing folder or the org quota is exhausted. permission error means your user is missing viewer on the project. ops can grant a scoped role.

infra-james: for the quota, ops will need to migrate the project to the EU billing folder or request extra quota. For resourcemanager, i'll ask ops to grant `roles/resourcemanager.projectViewer` temporarily. eva, can you run `gcloud projects get-iam-policy redwood-dev-sandbox --flatten='bindings[].members' --format='table(bindings.role)'` and paste output?

eva: output: `Permission denied: resource (projects/redwood-dev-sandbox) or requestor does not have permission.`

ops-lee: okay i've granted `roles/resourcemanager.projectViewer` to eva@redwood.com for redwood-dev-sandbox. also opened ticket CLD-2401 to migrate project under EU billing folder and CLD-2402 to request additional IN_USE_ADDRESSES quota for eu-west1. expect ~48h for quota increase.

eva: thanks — after viewer role terraform gets past project checks but now fails when enabling `compute.googleapis.com` in eu-west1: `API not enabled for project` even though console shows it enabled.

marta: weird; sometimes API enablement lags across org policies if project is still in the wrong billing folder. ops, did the migration already?

ops-lee: migration pending (CLD-2401). interim fix: i can enable the API at the organization level for that project or grant you a service account with the proper enabled APIs to run the provisioning. which do you prefer?

eva: temporary SA works for me so onboarding isn't blocked. what's the SA name?

ops-lee: creating `onboard-ci@redwood-devops.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and granting `roles/compute.networkAdmin` + `roles/compute.viewer`. i'll give you impersonation rights: `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on that SA for 48h.

cloud-onboard-bot: Reminder: After ops gives SA access, re-run `gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=onboard-ci@redwood-devops.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and then `terraform apply` with GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN set.

eva: impersonation works and terraform progressed further. thanks all. a separate quick Q: i also need AWS dev account CLI access — AWS SSO login works but `aws sts assume-role` for infra role keeps failing with AccessDenied. anyone seen SSO->assume role glitches?

ops-lee: depending on how the permission set maps, the role might require session tags or the trust policy expects the SSO principal. file a short update on the Cloud Access ticket listing the AWS account id and role arn and add note `cli-sso-tags: team=infra,project=sandbox`. we'll patch the permission set.

marta: security note: we prefer not to allow iam:CreateRole or broad iam perms from SSO by default. if terraform needs to create roles, ops will either pre-create them or grant narrowly scoped permissions with conditions. include terraform module path in the ticket so ops can pre-prepare resources.
